Built · 26 August 2026

The project tables, and a function that submits

These are screenshots of the real platform, not a drawing. Every table below came out of the built file a minute ago, at the width a pane actually has, in whichever theme you are reading this in. Finance › FIN01, all three panes.

One table, one row shape. A deliverable is an outcome whose direction is = and whose target is Y/N — written by the platform, shown quietly, because a value nobody can change should not look like a field. The Type column says which kind a row is.

The score column says what it holds now, not what it is measured in — Performance on the deliverables and outcomes, Progress on the milestones. They are two different numbers answering two different questions: how well and how far.

The due date is off the deliverable-and-outcome tables and off the upload template, as you asked. It is not deleted: where a plan carries one it still decides whether a row is asked for this cycle and whether it is late — that reading moved under the row’s name rather than disappearing. Milestones keep their column, now as a month and a year: July 2026.

A supporting function can now submit to the SMO — and everything except the button was already built. The page already knew the right key, the tab already knew how to show a Submitted badge, and the server has been accepting a submission from a function since it was written. The control was simply never drawn.

That is worth knowing because the platform has been putting a dot on a function’s Performance tab saying a submission was owed — with nothing on the page that would clear it. That is fixed by the same change.

An In progress with no number was reading as nought (the message before this one). The score counted it as zero the instant a dropdown changed. It leaves the average now and the pane marks it Needs a % — and a row in that state is one of the two things that stops a submission.

Capability › Projects — the plan pane

Five columns and every cell answered. Rows 1–4 are deliverables: = and Y/N are written in quietly. Rows 5 and 6 are outcomes and carry their own direction and target. The milestone table keeps Name, Description, Owner and Due date — the four fields you specified, with the date now reading March 2026.

Capability › Performance — the scoreboard

Status holds the word for a deliverable and the figure for an outcome; Performance holds the number the score is built from, for both, so the score column runs down one edge. Row 3 is overdue and says so under its name — that reading used to live in the due-date cell and moved rather than disappeared. Row 4 was delivered early: it is due December, it reads 100%, and it counts. Row 6 is not due and nothing has been said about it: dimmed, and marked as such.

Capability › Reporting — where the figures are entered

A deliverable picks a status and the per-cent follows — 100 for Delivered, 0 for Not started, a box only for In progress, which is the whole of “in progress requires a per-cent of completion”. An outcome types a figure and its per-cent is computed against the target. Row 6 is the fix: not due, dimmed, marked Not due — and the box is live, so it can be reported early. The tally reads what you owe this cycle, not everything in the plan.

The row that owes a number — Reporting, with one In progress on each table

Row 1 and milestone 1 have both said In progress and stopped there. The box is open, the mark says Needs a %, and the tally reads 7 of 9 rather than 9 of 9. Neither row is counted as nought and neither is counted at all — they are outstanding. Type a number and the mark goes and the figure appears.

Capability › Reporting — the bar, with Submit on it

Submit to the SMO, in the same place a unit has it — one submission per function, covering all its capabilities. It refuses on two things and says which: a row that said In progress and never said how far, and a figure at risk or off track with no note. That second rule is the unit’s own, and it blocks every unit but one in the demo today — so a function being blocked is faithful, not over-strict. Once it goes through, the bar reads Submitted with Reopen my report beside it.

Setup › Running the cycle — the SMO's board

A submission the SMO cannot see anywhere is half a feature, so functions are rows in the same table. The three count columns turned out to be three layers, not two vocabularies — a unit's are what we are judged on · what we measure · the work, and a function has the same three: key objectives, its outcomes, and its deliverables and milestones. So the counts read down the page against each other. The first attempt gave the functions their own column strip and the words collided; hover any count for the specific one.

What is behind it

  • Nobody’s score moved, and it is asserted rather than promised: the check strips every per-cent and compares Execution’s old formula against the new one across all eight capabilities. Identical, eight times.
  • The new rule is asserted from the failing side. I put the old behaviour back three times — the milestone lock, the Performance dash, the status pill — and the check went red for each. The first version of it stayed green on a reverted build, because FIN01 has no not-due milestone at all, so the check now makes the four cases rather than hoping the demo carries them.
  • A workbook downloaded before today still uploads. Its Kind column is read and ignored; its deliverables simply have no date, which is now true of all of them.
  • The full sweep is clean — every page as every viewer, no console errors.

What I would still put in front of you

  • The outcome sheet keeps its date column, deliberately. Taking it out too would stop a plan ever saying when an outcome is measured, and “not asked until Q4” has been in the product since the capability model existed. Say the word if you want it gone as well.
  • The database round trip is not run. Migration 023 needs a live Postgres, which this session does not have. I would want that green before this reaches production.
  • Reporting is seven columns now the date has gone. Still the widest table in the product, on the page somebody fills in under time pressure. The lever to make it six is reading the status out of the per-cent instead of asking both — on the table if you want it.
  • The server had never been asked a question about this. There was no control, so no test had a reason to exist — the fn: branch could have accepted anybody and nothing would have noticed. It is now tested at both ends: a function head may submit their own, and may not submit another’s.
  • The Notes column says “1 need notes”. That is the unit half’s existing wording, now visible on seven more rows. A grammar slip rather than a design one, and both halves say it identically — but correcting a label is your call, so it is written down rather than quietly changed.
  • The review deck still carries a Due date column on its deliverables-and-outcomes table. You named the tables and the upload templates; the deck was not mentioned, and a column on a projector that is absent in the product is the kind of drift worth deciding rather than letting happen. Yours to say.
  • The same not-due lock is still on a unit’s tactics table, which I have not touched because you did not ask about it. It is the same fault and the same one-line shape of fix. Yours to say.
  • Still unfixed from before: a project’s drag handles are bound to nothing — sortAttr() is defined and applied to neither table. What a drop between a deliverable and an outcome should mean is a decision, not a bug fix.
